subject: Production: med-summit-prod throttle feedback loop (urgent)
messages:
From: Alyssa Cho <alyssa.cho@medhealth.com>
To: marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Cc: support@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-05-21T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Production spike: med-summit-prod 429/timeout surge

Hi Marcus —

We're seeing a sudden burst of 429s and timeouts against med-summit-prod starting ~08:50 PDT. Error rate jumped to ~48% and median latency doubled; customers are hitting timeouts. Our sidecar traces show a lot of requests failing with 429s from the quota enforcement layer (org->project mapping shows project: med-summit-prod / client_id: mh-summit).

We've attached a short CSV with per-minute error counts and an example trace (error_dump_20270521.csv). This started immediately after the org tiering cutover this morning — can you confirm whether any tiering or alias mapping changed? Execs are on the line; we need a mitigation plan now.

Impact: multiple caregivers' workflows blocked, three urgent incident pages so far.

Thanks,
Alyssa
Alyssa Cho
SRE, MedHealth Systems

Attachment: error_dump_20270521.csv
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Alyssa Cho <alyssa.cho@medhealth.com>, support@medhealth.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-05-21T09:23:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production spike: med-summit-prod 429/timeout surge

Alyssa — thanks for the flag and sorry for the interruption. Looping in the infra/ops team.

Immediate plan (next 30 mins):
- I'll authorize an emergency quota bump for med-summit-prod and temporarily route requests to the enterprise-rate fallback variant to suppress 429s.
- Marissa/Karthik to validate org->project tiering mappings and rollback any bad alias changes.
- We'll tail the quota-service logs and provide rolling status updates every 15 minutes.

Can you confirm whether you see any client-side retry amplification (rapid retries from customer clients)? If so, set client-side backoff to 5s while we stabilize.

Opening INF ticket and HubSpot record: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/record/HS-9863.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: marcus_lin@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-05-21T09:32:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production spike: med-summit-prod 429/timeout surge — initial triage

Quick triage notes:
- I pulled the tiering config diff from this morning's cutover. There's an alias mapping that replaced medhealth/main -> med-summit-prod with tier key "starter" instead of the expected "enterprise_1". That will immediately apply much lower per-project quotas. Patch attached (org-tiering-diff.patch) showing the delta.
- No runtime code changes; this is purely a config mapping regression in the cutover job.
- I recommend two immediate actions: 1) rollback the alias delta to restore enterprise tier; 2) apply emergency quota bump for med-summit-prod to 3x current allocation until rollback completes.

I've prepared the rollback commands and a safe mutation plan — see rollout_commands.txt. Karthik, can you own the rollback and signal when done?

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Engineering Manager, Routing & Quotas

Attachment: org-tiering-diff.patch
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: Alyssa Cho <alyssa.cho@medhealth.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-05-21T09:45:00-07:00
Subject: Exec note: MedHealth impacting production; approval request for emergency quota bump

Team —
MedHealth execs are on the line and asking for SLA remediation if we don't stabilize within 90 minutes. I'm requesting approval to proceed with the emergency quota bump and immediate rollback of the morning cutover alias. Impact window estimate: 20–35 minutes from start of rollback to normalized 429 rates.

Rationale: config cutover inadvertently demoted med-summit-prod to a lower tier causing per-project rate limits to surface; this in turn triggered client retry bursts which amplified the 429 flood. The quickest customer-impact fix is a temporary quota increase + rollback.

Please confirm approvals ASAP so we can move. I'll also prepare a customer-facing incident note for transparency.

—Marcus
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: marcus_lin@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, Alyssa Cho <alyssa.cho@medhealth.com>
Date: 2027-05-21T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production spike: med-summit-prod 429/timeout surge — mitigation applied

On Fri, May 21, 2027 at 09:32 Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Looping in the infra/ops team.

Rollback applied at 10:01 PDT and emergency quota bump executed at 10:02 PDT (applied +300% for med-summit-prod). Monitoring shows 429 rate falling from 48% -> 6% within 6 minutes; median latency back to baseline within 10 minutes.

I also disabled immediate client retries via config gate (suggested by Marcus) to reduce amplification — please confirm if MedHealth adjusted their SDK backoff as well.

Next steps:
- Postmortem scheduled (INF-2247) for 0500 UTC tomorrow to cover root cause and process gaps.
- We'll add a safety check to the tiering cutover job to prevent demotions without an explicit approval flag.

Rollout artifacts: rollout_commands.txt attached.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Site Reliability Engineer

Attachment: rollout_commands.txt
From: Alyssa Cho <alyssa.cho@medhealth.com>
To: marcus_lin@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-05-21T11:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production spike: med-summit-prod 429/timeout surge — thanks

Thanks Marcus/Karthik/Marissa — we see normal traffic again and error rate is back to baseline.

MedHealth will share a short impact summary (customers affected and estimated lost throughput) after we finish internal tallies. We appreciate the quick turnaround and the plan for a postmortem. Please include us on INF-2247 notes and the cutover safeguard design.

Best,
Alyssa
